last_debrief: STORY SO FAR: Sat 09-05, day 24, and the session opened with the machine broken rather than the learner. The auto-drain dispatched the standing compound-verb order and the soak lane published TWELVE SECONDS of intro and outro over an empty sheet — to the feed, to his lock screen, order stamped delivered, exit 0. He took the @build hat himself: 'fix it first.' Root cause was one schema key (SOAK_SCHEMA said `ta` where the mandate and three readers say `say`, and the agent path eats undeclared keys); the guard that should have caught it had a line-anchored needle and had been green over it forever. Fixed, plus two more of the same bug it had never been pointed at, plus a runtime floor that refuses to publish an empty loop. The real dose then went out: 6.3 minutes, four threads, twelve lines, tail verb the only moving part. HE HAS NOT HEARD IT YET. THEN THE TABLE REHEARSAL, owed since 09-01 and deferred three times. Masks at full speed. THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE WHOLE SESSION: three swings at an elder in ten minutes and NOT ONE -nga on any of them. Athai with the ladle -> 'podhum, then vendaam' (podhum instant and cold, but that word has been his for ten years; vendaanga was owed). Maami standing while he sat -> 'ukarala', which is not 'sit down' at all, it is DIDN'T SIT — he handed her a negative. Same beat, asked to make her eat, he gave 'saapten' — correct Tamil, correct answer to her question, and he let her walk back to the kitchen unfed. The words are all there. The respect ending is what is not firing, and it is the exact morphology the declining set needs — every line in the campaign's through-line is spoken TO an elder. Named it once, set the trap one beat later: 'ukkarunga. Saapdunga.' Both endings, no hunting. HINTED, not cold — I had just handed him the form. The real test is an unannounced ambush days from now; hold it. AND I GOT ONE WRONG, HE CORRECTED ME, AND HIS VERSION IS SHARPER. Cousin at speed: 'naan kadaikku poi paathuttu vandhutten, avan illa.' Asked where I am standing, he said 'en route' and I logged it as the tail dying again — third session of come-go-direction. He came back with 'store went looked and came, he was not there?' — every verb, in order, INCLUDING the tail. So the compound is NOT the hole. He parsed all three verbs and still could not put my body in the room: vandhutten does not mean 'came', it means CAME TO WHERE YOU AND I ARE. The direction hangs on the speaker, and that is deixis, not morphology. This refines come-go-direction rather than repeating it — check what he actually decoded before re-ordering the dose. HE ASKED FOR A DECOMPOSITION UNPROMPTED and it was the best beat of the hour: 'I don't know the word paapom.' paar -> paaru / paathen / paathuttu / paapom. One root, four tails, and he had already translated paathuttu himself thirty seconds earlier. Decomposition on demand is still his highest-yield move. THE MISSION WENT UNCOLLECTED — adhukku appuram twice in one story. He walked in and went straight to the broken machine, so the debrief never happened. Collect it next open before anything else; two sessions of that op landing is real evidence and I have not banked the second one. வா IS STILL HELD OUT OF EVERY PRODUCTION SLOT. The ambush is unspent. Today's ear beat used it in MY mouth only, which does not spend it. TOMORROW OFFERED: the Gauntlet, earned — he took a full rehearsal at speed on a day that started with an outage. Low-power twin: the compound tape he has not heard yet, by ear. TONIGHT'S MISSION, and the trigger is the one thing that house does without fail: someone will put more on his plate, unasked, at the next meal. The op is ONE WORD and it is the ending — vendaanga, not vendaam. If it is athai holding the ladle, the stretch is to turn it back on her in the same breath: vendaanga, neenga saapdunga. An answer, in the response slot he is strong in, off a trigger the room speaks every single day. Collect it FIRST next open, along with the adhukku appuram debrief that never happened today.

soak_order.focus: THE -nga RESPECT ENDING, AND IT IS THE ONLY MOVING PART. Run MATCHED PAIRS on one verb at a time, the plain form then the -nga form, nothing else changing: ukkaaru / ukkaarunga, saapdu / saapdunga, vendaam / vendaanga, sollu / sollunga, vaa / vaanga. Same verb, same tense, same sentence around it; the ending must be the loudest thing in the line. Put each pair in an ordinary situation at a table or a doorway, with an elder on the receiving end of the -nga form. Do NOT permute the verb inside a pair, do NOT stack two endings, do NOT explain the politeness, and never name a rule. THIS BRIEF IS FOR YOU, NOT FOR HIM: say nothing in the intro, outro or any cue about what he got wrong, how often, or that this is a repair at all. No counts, no tally, no 'tonight you missed'. He is doing reps, not reading a report.
